## Historical audit: S0117

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 3 is available; citations below refer to its JSONL events and supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Line 15, student `model_request`, chars [0,198169) | The explicit goal was an editable, separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, matching camera, proportions, colors and occlusions without using the photograph as a texture. The student’s *interpretation* was an electronics workbench with monitor, instruments, keyboard, lamp, drawers and leads; the image itself is not visible to this audit. |
| Line 15, embedded student programs and runner feedback, chars [0,198169) | The first program constructed multiple grouped objects from colored boxes, rods and a ball. It specified object rotations, a camera and lights. The runner reported steps 1 and 2 successful and supplied render paths. After step 1, the student diagnosed overly wide framing, reversed perspective and washed-out regions, then changed camera offset and lens, enlarged the monitor and lamp, and darkened surfaces and lighting. These are student diagnoses, not independent image verification. |
| Line 17, student `model_response`, chars [0,12755); line 18, `execute`, chars [0,13402) | After receiving step 2 feedback, the student identified low framing, monitor cropping/perspective and a thin, level lamp. The complete step-3 program lowered the camera target, moved and rotated the monitor, changed keyboard pose, grouped and rotated a deeper lamp shade, and reduced illumination/exposure. The execution event contains that program; this was not an empty patch. |
| Line 19, `execution_result`, chars [0,99741); lines 20–21, `select`, chars [0,58) and [0,59) | Step 3 returned `ok: true`, with a finished render, saved image and Blender scene. Step 3 was selected twice. This establishes **technical build/render success and selection**, not geometric or visual correctness. No formal similarity score or final quality judgment is visible. |
| Line 16, student `codex_session`, chars [0,3821) | The session was read-only, with external tools disabled and zero recorded tool calls. Iteration was autonomous within the supplied render-feedback interface. No separate teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher input is visible in this chunk; adoption of any such input is therefore unestablished. |

**Scene checks and uncertainty.** The code provides evidence of multiple object groups, distinct colors, and intended connections such as a monitor stand and lamp arm/shade. It uses primitive color finishes rather than an observable image-texture workflow; actual texture fidelity and physical contact are unverified. Rotations and camera/light settings show attempted pose and framing control, but the reference and renders are not available as images here. Whether the stated discrepancies were real or the changes improved them remains unresolved. The saved render alone does not establish correctness; neither algorithm failure nor technical interruption is shown in this excerpt, and the overall outcome beyond it is unknown.

**Transferable lesson:** Separate runtime success from visual validation, and distinguish global camera hypotheses from local object edits. **Task-specific lesson:** The monitor, keyboard and lamp adjustments were responses to this student’s particular workbench interpretation, not verified general solutions.
